info.title: Matinee AI API
info.description: Infrastructure for AI-powered digital economies. Generated from src/api/ — see docs/api/. This document is the contract between the frontend, backend, SDKs and third-party developers (Phase 9 §1).

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Session lifecycle. No public signup — Phase 7 §5.5 gives two entry paths, both elsewhere.

tags.name: Access requests
tags.description: The door. Phase 7 §5.5: there is no public signup, so this is how an organization begins.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: The tenant.

tags.name: Team
tags.description: Membership and roles. The second entry path (Phase 7 §5.5) is here.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: End users of a business. Phase 7 §11 forbids merging these with platform users.

tags.name: Wallets
tags.description: Holders of balances. Balances themselves are derived from the ledger (ADR-0008).

tags.name: Ledger
tags.description: Double-entry postings. The invariants are enforced by the database regardless of caller (Phase 8 §66).

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: Digital assets. Blockchain is an optional adapter (ADR-0009), so deployment is a separate, gated operation.

tags.name: Rewards
tags.description: Programmes, versions and rules. Editing an active rule creates a draft (Phase 7 §14.3).

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Business events in, platform events out. ADR-0012 makes duplicates expected.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Signed outbound delivery with the Phase 7 §19.3 retry schedule.

tags.name: Developers
tags.description: Projects, keys and usage.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: Read-only assistance plus a proposal-and-approval boundary. Phase 7 §17.5.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Served from aggregates. Phase 7 §21 forbids querying transactional tables directly.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description: Read-only. Phase 8 makes audit_logs append-only with a trigger, so there is no write endpoint to specify.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: In-app notifications and delivery preferences.

tags.name: Security
tags.description: Alerts, devices and sessions.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: One query across seven resource types, tenant filtered.

tags.name: Batch
tags.description: Bulk writes. Every item is authorized and idempotency-keyed independently.

tags.name: Digital Assets
tags.description: The Digital Asset Engine's public surface. §2: infrastructure is chosen after the business purpose, so none of these endpoints requires a chain.

tags.name: Blockchain Transactions
tags.description: The §24 transaction lifecycle, read and operated on. Empty in every environment — nothing has been submitted to a network.

tags.name: Blockchain Networks
tags.description: The network registry. Returns an empty collection: §22 says start with one or two networks based on actual customer need, and no adapter exists to make one real.

tags.name: Treasury
tags.description: §17.1's seven accounts, served from the ledger rather than from a treasury table — ADR-0008 keeps every balance in the ledger, and a treasury balance held elsewhere would be a second source of truth.

tags.name: Approvals
tags.description: §34 — the human decision point for high-risk operations. The four-eyes rule is enforced beneath this API: the database refuses a decision from the user who raised the request.

tags.name: AI Agents
tags.description: §9 — a configured AI worker with a role, permissions, tools and operating rules. §3 caps its authority at the invoking user's.

tags.name: AI Conversations
tags.description: §49 — the Business Assistant surface. Phase 9 §19 opened this group; §66.2 completes it.

tags.name: AI Runs
tags.description: §12 — one agent task. §41 calls the record a trace.

tags.name: AI Actions
tags.description: §29–§30 — where everything the AI cannot do on its own authority arrives for a human decision.

tags.name: AI Knowledge
tags.description: §18–§23. Phase 8 built the tables and pgvector; nothing is indexed, because there is no embedding provider.

tags.name: AI Memory
tags.description: §24–§26 — memory must be controlled and transparent, which means the user can see and delete it.

tags.name: AI Prompts
tags.description: §27 and §57 — prompts as versioned product assets rather than string literals in application code.

tags.name: AI Evaluations
tags.description: §43–§44 — every production agent is evaluated before activation, and the golden set is what it is evaluated against.

tags.name: AI Usage
tags.description: §39–§40 — AI usage becomes expensive without controls, so cost is a first-class read.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: §1 — the automation layer that connects triggers, conditions, actions, AI decisions and approvals. §26 puts the definition in versions, so a workflow row is identity, status and risk.

tags.name: Workflow Versions
tags.description: §27 — eleven fields per version, six of them inside the §64 definition document. §3.4 makes a published one immutable.

tags.name: Workflow Validation
tags.description: §29 — twelve rules. Six are decidable from the definition alone; six need a runtime, a connector or a live endpoint, and one of those cannot be decided at publish time at all.

tags.name: Workflow Simulation
tags.description: §30 — evaluate a workflow against a sample event without changing production data.

tags.name: Workflow Lifecycle
tags.description: §26 and §80 — publishing freezes a version; pausing stops the next execution rather than recording an intention to.

tags.name: Workflow Execution
tags.description: §6 — the manual and API trigger types. The other five start a workflow without a request.

tags.name: Workflow Executions
tags.description: §33 and §43 — one independent run, and the history that makes it explicable. §13.1 keeps the state in a row rather than a process, which is why §80's delayed workflows survive a restart.

tags.name: Workflow Approvals
tags.description: §15 — execution stops here until a human decides. The third approval surface in the platform, after Phase 10 §67 and Phase 11 §29; ADR-0026 records why the tables are separate and the four-eyes rule is not.
